about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Nothing new on the supply side overnight: US harvest reports describe uneven yields after weather extremes, and the dollar is still the main drag. Dec is in delivery week near 75.8, so the tradeable read is Mar/May; watch high-grade certs, which would add to delivered pressure rather than ease it.
events: Farm Progress says weather extremes left mixed US cotton yields (Farm Progress)
Cotton recovers part of the week's losses on Thursday (Barchart)
Firm dollar weighs on cotton demand (ADMIS)

sugar.fundamental: The sell-off is Brazil-led: a sliding real (near 5.90) makes Brazilian exports cheaper and pushes Mar toward 17.15, a seven-week low. The only offset is the poor French beet harvest, which tightens EU white supply at the margin but does not change the Centre-South picture.
events: Real weakness drives raw sugar to a 7-week low (Barchart)
Tereos cuts its outlook after a weak French beet crop (Investing.com)

coffee.fundamental: No fresh ICE certified-stock or Brazil deliverability data since the low certs reading earlier this week; the near-term support from tight exchange stocks is intact. Smaller Colombian exports helped Thursday, but the weaker real keeps Brazilian farmer selling a headwind.
events: Real slide weighs on Brazil-origin softs (Barchart)

cocoa.fundamental: Rising ICE stocks still weigh, but two supportive threads are building: European physical premiums are firming as buyers prepare for EU deforestation rules, and the late Ivorian main crop risks port congestion that would slow arrivals. Thursday's short-covering bounce fits that mix.
events: Cocoa dearer in Europe as traders prepare for EUDR (Bloomberg)
Delayed Ivory Coast crop may congest ports ahead of EU rules (Reuters via Nation)
Mar cocoa jumps ~3% on short covering (ICE)
